question: The marked price of a shirt is ₹500. If the shopkeeper offers a 20% discount, what is the selling price of the shirt?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Discount = 20% = 1 ÷ 5 (where MP is 5 units, Discount is 1 unit)

Selling Price (SP) = 5 − 1 = 4 units

Given 5 units = ₹500

⇒ 1 unit = 500 ÷ 5 = ₹100

⇒ SP (4 units) = 4 × 100 = ₹400

**∴ The correct answer is ₹400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹500

Discount Percentage = 20%

**Formula Used:**

Discount Value = MP × (Discount% ÷ 100)

Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount Value

 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 MP = ₹500
 
 
 SP = ?
 (₹400)

 

 
 − 20% Discount
 − ₹100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Discount Value = 500 × (20 ÷ 100)

⇒ Discount Value = ₹100

⇒ SP = 500 − 100

⇒ SP = ₹400

**∴ The correct answer is ₹400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price (MP)

It is the price on the label of an article. Any discount offered to the customer is always calculated strictly on the Marked Price.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the equivalent single discount percentage is computed as: (a + b − a × b ÷ 100)%.

Direct Formula for CP and MP Relation

The direct ratio between Cost Price (CP) and Marked Price (MP) is derived as: CP ÷ MP = (100 − Discount%) ÷ (100 + Profit%).
